entry.title: Hymnarium Digitale
entry.content:
On the Feast of the Nativity of the Virgin Mary, I am delighted to present to the international scholarly community the first stage of a major research project devoted to the study and recensio of ecclesiastical hymns.

Entitled Hymnarium Digitale, the project reflects the dual nature of this undertaking. On the one hand, it seeks to provide a comprehensive catalogue of hymnographic production, approached from both synchronic and diachronic perspectives. On the other, by harnessing the potential of digital technologies, it aims to develop a dynamic infrastructure for the exploration and analysis of textual traditions.

The first resources now available to users include an alphabetical catalogue of the incipit of the hymns collected so far, together with a search interface that makes it possible to conduct cross-referenced queries across textual data, sources, and authors.

Further tools and resources will be progressively made available over the coming months, as the project continues to develop.

entry.title: Matins Readings
entry.content:
In the latest issue of Ephemerides Liturgicae, my extensive study on the biblical, patristic, and hagiographic pericopes contained in the 1957 edition of the “Breviarium Ambrosianum” was published.

On the biblical side, one notes the substantial preservation of the ordo set out by Beroldus in the 12th century; the selection of patristic texts is marked by a prevalence of Ambrosian and Augustinian writings, though other authors are not absent; the lives of the saints, on the other hand, have undergone continual processes of updating in periods following the Council of Trent. The composite form of this document is a valuable historical witness to a multifaceted stratification, whose study may open the way to further investigations.
entry.summary: A study on the matins readings in the last edition of the Ambrosian Breviary

entry.title: NLP for Digital Humanities
entry.content:
Today my recent research was published in the scientific journal Umanistica Digitale.

This article offers a survey of recent studies on the application of Natural Language Processing techniques to classical philology, with particular emphasis on Latin epic poetry of the 1st century AD. Although originally designed for the analysis of modern languages, the algorithms developed in computational linguistics over the past three decades – ranging from Latent Semantic Allocation and Latent Dirichlet Allocation to the more recent Transformer models based on Neural Networks – have transformed intertextual research through the practice of Topic Extraction. Particular attention is given to cases aimed at detecting situational correspondences even in the absence of co-occurring vocabulary. The examples discussed confirm both the efficacy of this approach and the convergence between ‘traditional’ philological methods and computational-linguistic techniques.
entry.summary: Applications of Digital Analysis Techniques to Classical Languages and Literatures

entry.title: Database of Latin Compounds
entry.content:
During the 23rd International Colloquium of Latin Linguistics , Andrea Brunello, Giovanni Torresin, and I had the great pleasure of presenting to the scholarly community the final version of the database containing the linguistic material that Renato Oniga and I had collected over more than a decade of research.

Thanks to the invaluable expertise and contributions of Andrea Brunello and Giovanni Torresin, we developed a Neo4j graph database that supports complex Cypher queries , enabling the extraction of a substantial amount of linguistic data concerning the typology and frequency of nominal compounds. These data can be employed not only to investigate the language of Latin authors but also to explore potential correlations between literary genre and lexical choices.

The latest issue of the journal Lingue Antiche e Moderne contains an article outlining both the theoretical foundations of the research and the practical implementation of the database.
entry.summary: Neo4j graph database about Latin nominal compounds

entry.title: Between Linguistics and Stylistics
entry.content:
In the last weeks, the volume of proceedings of the 22nd International Colloquium on Latin Linguistics, held in Prague in June 2023, was published.

Renato Oniga and I participated presenting a paper titled Between Linguistics and Stylistics: Nominal Compounding and Literary Genre in Latin.

Here is a brief summary of the contents of our talk.

The collection of linguistic data from the 3rd century B.C. to the 5th century A.D. made possible a typological classification of Latin nominal compounds based on a simplified Construction Grammar perspective.

This work showed evident links between the different types of compounds and the literary genre of the text in which they are used. Certain types of compounds – i.e. bahuvrīhi and most of nomina agentis – are mainly attested in high poetry, and especially epics, while other types – i.e. nomina actionis and nominal abstracta – are primarily used in prose.

Essentially, although morphological constructions are abstract entities whose existence in the linguistic competence of the speakers may only be supposed, they produce evident consequences in the stylistic nature of Latin literary texts.
entry.summary: Nominal Compounding and Literary Genre in Latin

entry.title: Phrasal Verbs from Latin to Friulian

link.title: Phrasal Verbs from Latin to Friulian

entry.content:
In 2022, I held a research fellowship at the University of Udine, in collaboration with the Friulian Philological Society — Società Filologica Friulana. During this period, I studied Friulian phrasal verbs, focusing in particular on the typological shift that occurred in the transition from Latin to the Romance languages.

Whereas Latin exhibits a clearly verb-framed typology, the Romance languages are generally characterized as satellite-framed. Traces of this transition can already be identified in Latin, as demonstrated by the documentary evidence I collected. This material was presented at an online seminar held at the “Centre de Lingüística Teòrica” of the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona in May 2022.

A revised version of the talk, prepared jointly with Paolo Lorusso and Renato Oniga, was subsequently published as an article in L’analisi linguistica e letteraria.
entry.summary: Transition from verb-framed to satellite-framed typology between Latin and Romance languages

entry.title: Epenthesis in Latin
entry.content:
In September 2021, Stony Brook University (NY) hosted a conference devoted to epenthesis.

Renato Oniga and I participated presenting a paper on this phenomenon in Latin.

Starting with the concise treatment of this subject provided by Max Niedermann in his Précis de phonétique historique du Latin, we first examined how ancient grammarians explained the phenomenon, and then we investigated those linguistic evidences that may explain why Latin speakers resorted to epenthesis in specific phonetic contexts.

The results of our research were subsequently published in the prestigious Journal of Latin Linguistics.
entry.summary: Development of consonant epenthesis in Latin from the Archaic period to the Romance outcomes

entry.title: Dante Alighieri and Friulian
entry.content:
In 2021, the seven-hundredth anniversary of Dante Alighieri’s death prompted the Società Filologica Friulana to devote a substantial part of the eight edition of the Setemane de Culture Furlane to this author and his literary production.

Invited to contribute to a conference entitled “Ces fastu crudeliter accentuando eructuant. Dante e il Friuli settecento anni dopo”, I examined whether and to what extent, the linguistic theories expressed in Dante’s De vulgari eloquentia can still be regarded as relevant when considered in the light of recent developments in this field of research.

A revised version of my contribution was subsequently published in the conference proceedings.
entry.summary: Dante's linguistic theories compared with contemporary linguistics and dialectology

entry.title: Two Studies on Pliny the Younger

link.title: Two Studies on Pliny the Younger

entry.content:
In 2021, two of my contributions on the works of Pliny the Younger were published. I have held a particular admiration for this author, owing not only to the depth and breadth of his subjects but also to the sophistication and refinement of his literary style.

With regard to the former aspect, I presented a paper entitled “Ville in Plinio il Giovane, orizzonte reale o spazio ideale?” at the international conference Centro e periferia nella letteratura latina di età imperiale, organized in January 2021 by the DIUM of the University of Udine. A revised version of the paper was subsequently published in the conference proceedings.

My interest in the linguistic dimension of Pliny’s writing led me to investigate the nominal compounds employed in his Panegyricus to Trajan, one of the masterpieces of Latin oratory. These lexical items are witness of the highly refined and sophisticated character of Pliny’s diction, which constitutes one of the most distinctive features of his literary production. Then, the results of this research were published in the prestigious journal Paideia.

Although the two studies originated from different epistemological perspectives, they both contribute to a deeper comprehension of the human and literary figure of Pliny the Younger.
entry.summary: Nominal compounds in the Panegyric and villas in the Letters illustrate two aspects of Pliny's production
